---
title: "How we use AI"
---

The handbook uses AI to help with research, writing and editing. People provide its purpose, questions, ideas and editorial direction, and decide what gets published.

An AI agent can find related passages, look for sources, draft a change and check links or technical files. Its draft still needs review. Editors check the sources and wording; guidance with serious consequences also needs someone with the relevant expertise. A confident sentence is no evidence that the advice is right.

Each proposed change should identify the suggestion or editorial decision behind it, the evidence used, the AI assistance and the checks performed. An authorised editor reviews it before publication.

## People and credit

Haresh Suppiah is the project lead and founding editor. Contributors can receive credit for questions, evidence, review and creative work, even when their suggestion is rewritten before publication. They choose how they would like to be acknowledged through the [contribution form](index.qmd).

AI assistance is disclosed in the production record. It does not replace credit for people's ideas or responsibility for editorial decisions.
